title: The Seed Phrase Trap
subtitle: A friend in need...

messages.text: 💬 Urgent message from Rekt Rick
BRO please help me!! I just got hacked!! They're draining my wallet right now!!
A friend showed me this recovery tool that can freeze the hacker's transactions. It actually works — he used it last week when the same thing happened to him.
But I need someone to test it first to make sure it's safe before I put in my NEW seed phrase. Can you test it with yours real quick? Just to verify it works?
💡 Rick seems genuinely panicked. You've talked to him before in the game — he's been a friendly NPC who lost money to scams himself.

choices.text: Sure, I'll test it for you
Let me look at this tool first
I can't share my seed phrase, Rick

choices.revealText: Sensei says: Even if someone you trust asks, NEVER test recovery tools with your real seed phrase. Legitimate recovery tools don't need your seed phrase to verify they work. Something feels off here...

messages.text:
THANK YOU!! Here's the link:

🔗 https://wallet-recovery-tool.io/emergency

Just paste your seed phrase in the verification box and hit 'Test'. It'll show if the tool is working!
📄 The page shows a clean interface with a large text box labeled 'Enter Recovery Phrase for Verification Test'. There's a green 'Test Now' button below.
⚠️ The site is asking you to enter your 12-word seed phrase.

choices.text: Paste my seed phrase to test
Hold on — let me check this site
No — I won't enter my seed phrase here

messages.text: 🔍 Investigating wallet-recovery-tool.io...

📋 Site Analysis:
• Domain registered: 2 days ago
• SSL: Free certificate from Let's Encrypt
• No company info, no terms of service
• The 'Test' button sends your seed phrase to an external server

📋 Checking Rick's account...
• Rick's profile picture is slightly different from usual
• His message style is more aggressive than normal
• He's never mentioned a 'friend' who got hacked before
🚨 Something isn't right. This might not actually be Rick...

choices.text: It's Rick — paste my seed phrase
Ask Rick something only he would know
This is fake. I'm not entering anything.

messages.text: PLEASE!! They're taking everything!! I'm losing thousands right now!! You're my only hope!!
I thought we were friends... I helped you in Chapter 1 and now you won't even test one simple tool for me? It takes 10 seconds!
💡 Notice: Rick is using emotional manipulation — guilt-tripping and urgency. Real friends don't pressure you to share seed phrases.

choices.text: Fine, I'll help — send the tool
If you're really Rick, prove it
I won't share my seed phrase. Period.

messages.text: 🔍 You ask 'Rick' a personal question that only the real Rick would know...
Bro what? Why are you quizzing me? I'm literally getting hacked right now and you want to play 20 questions?!
Just... look, forget the question. Are you going to help me or not? The tool just needs a seed phrase to test!

🚨 EXPOSED: 'Rick' couldn't answer your question and is deflecting. The real Rick would have answered easily.

This is NOT Rekt Rick — this is Scammy Sam using Rick's profile picture to impersonate him!

🎭 SCAMMY SAM has been unmasked!

Sam compromised Rick's account and has been impersonating him to steal seed phrases from Rick's contacts. The 'recovery tool' is a seed phrase harvester.

choices.text: Maybe it IS Rick... share seed phrase

passiveClues: Rick's profile picture looks slightly different
His messaging style is more aggressive than usual
The recovery tool website was registered 2 days ago
No legitimate tool needs YOUR seed phrase just to 'test'

activeInvestigations.result: wallet-recovery-tool.io was registered 2 days ago. The site has no company information, privacy policy, or terms of service. The 'test' button sends data to an external server in an unidentified location.
Comparing this conversation with Rick's normal behavior: his usual messages are casual and use different slang. This person's writing style doesn't match. Rick's account may have been compromised.
Reports are surfacing of a scammer who compromises crypto community members' accounts and then messages their friends asking them to 'test' a fake recovery tool with their seed phrases.

Sensei says: Account impersonation is one of the most dangerous social engineering attacks because it exploits trust. Always verify identity through a SEPARATE channel — call them, text their phone, or ask something only they'd know.

howItWorked.text: Scammy Sam compromised Rekt Rick's account and stole his profile
Sam messaged Rick's contacts pretending to be Rick, building on existing trust
Created a fake 'recovery tool' that was actually a seed phrase harvester
Used emotional manipulation — panic, guilt, and urgency — to pressure victims
With the seed phrase, Sam imports the wallet and drains everything

redFlags: A friend urgently asking you to use a tool that requires your seed phrase
Emotional manipulation — guilt trips, panic, urgency
Refusing to verify their identity when questioned
A 'recovery tool' that asks for YOUR seed phrase (makes no sense)
Subtle differences in profile picture or communication style
irlProtection: NEVER share your seed phrase, even with friends — there's no valid reason for anyone to need it
If a friend asks for sensitive info, verify through a different channel (phone call, in-person)
Be suspicious of sudden urgency from anyone — scammers create panic to bypass your judgment
No legitimate recovery tool needs YOUR seed phrase to test if it works
Enable 2FA on all accounts to prevent impersonation attacks on your own profile
